Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:1.hebrew: א"ל רב המנונא - לעולא, היאך יוצאין לחולין בלא פדייה:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:1.english: Rav Hamnuna said to him - [Meaning,] to Ulla: How do [the saplings] become non-sacred without redemption?

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:2.hebrew: וכי קדושה שלהן להיכן הלכה - כלומר, היכי פקעה בכדי אע"פ שנקצצו:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:2.english: And where did their sanctity go? - That is to say, how does [their sanctity] cease for naught, even though they were cut down?

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:3.english: And is not one who says to a woman, "Today you are my wife" - [Saying] that she should be betrothed to me today.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:4.hebrew: ולמחר אי את אשתי - אע"פ שהתנה כך בשעת קידושין:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:4.english: And tomorrow you are not my wife - Even though he stipulated thus at the time of betrothal.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:5.hebrew: מי נפקא למחר בלא גט - ה"נ, אע"ג דנקצצו, היינו כמו למחר אין את אשתו, ולא נפקי בלא פדיון:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:1:5.english: Would she exit tomorrow without a bill of divorce - Here too, even though [the saplings] were cut down, that is like [saying] "tomorrow you are not his wife," and they do not exit [their sanctity] without redemption.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:2:1.hebrew: מי קא מדמית קדושת הגוף - וכו'. הני נטיעות דקדישי לפדייה, קדישי קדושת דמים, ולהכי פקעו מאחר שנקצצו. אבל אשה קדושת הגוף היא, ולהכי לא פקעה בכדי:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:2:1.english: Do you compare ... inherent sanctity - etc. These saplings, which are consecrated for redemption, are consecrated [with] sanctity of value, and therefore [their sanctity] departs once they are cut down. However, a woman is [a case of] inherent sanctity, and therefore [her sanctity] does not depart with nothing [being done].

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:1.hebrew: והתניא מי שאמר שור זה עולה כל ל' יום - שאם יקרב בתוך ל' יום, עולה; ואם לאחר ל' יום יקרב, יהא שלמים:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:1.english: But isn't it taught [in a baraita]: One who said, "This ox is a burnt-offering for all thirty days" - That if it is offered within thirty days, [it is] a burnt-offering; and if it is offered after thirty days, it shall be a peace-offering.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:2.hebrew: כל ל' יום הוי עולה - כמו שאמר, ולאחר ל' יצא מקדושת עולה והוי שלמים:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:2.english: All thirty days it is a burnt-offering - As he said; and after thirty [days] it leaves the sanctity of a burnt-offering and becomes a peace-offering.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:3.hebrew: ואמאי - נפקא מקדושת עולה? הא קדושת הגוף נינהו ופקעה בכדי, וקשיא לעולא דאמר קדושת הגוף לא פקעה בכדי:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:3:3.english: And why - [does it] leave the sanctity of a burnt-offering? Behold, these are [cases of] inherent sanctity, and [yet] it departs with nothing [being done], and this is a difficulty for Ulla, who said [that] inherent sanctity does not depart with nothing [being done].

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:4:1.english: Ulla would say to you: With what are we dealing here - [such] that the sanctity of the burnt-offering departs.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:4:2.hebrew: דאמר לדמי - דאמר הכי, תורת דמיו עולה כל ל' יום, לאחר שאפדנו ואקח בדליו עולה. להכי לאחר ל' יום פקעה בכדי, דקדושת דמים היא, אבל קדושת הגוף אכתי לא פקעה:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:4:2.english: [Where] he said [it] for [its] monetary value - That he said thus: "[Let it have] the status of its value [as] a burnt-offering for all thirty days — after I redeem it and buy a burnt-offering with its money." Therefore, after thirty days it departs on its own, for it is monetary sanctity, whereas inherent sanctity still does not depart.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:5:1.hebrew: א"ה - דמוקמת לה לדמי:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:5:1.english: If so - that you establish it [as referring] to [sanctity of] value.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:5:2.hebrew: אימא סיפא - דההיא: אמר שור זה לאחר שלשים יום עולה, ומעכשיו ועד שלשים יום שלמים — הכי הוי כדאמר איהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 29a:5:2.english: Say the latter clause - Of that [teaching, where] he said: "This ox [shall be] a burnt-offering after thirty days, and from now until thirty days [it shall be] a peace-offering" — so it is, as he said.

Rashi on Nedarim 29a:5:3.english: Granted, if you say - [that] the first clause [refers] to inherent sanctity and the latter clause [refers] to sanctity of value.

Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:1:1.hebrew: היום את אשתי ולמחר אי את אשתי מי נפקא בלא גט - וא"ת: ומנלן דצריך גט? וי"ל, דבפרק המגרש בגטין (דף פג:) מיבעיא לן גבי האומר לאשתו: "היום אי את אשתי ולמחר את אשתי", כלומר תהא מגורשת היום ולמחר לא תהא מגורשת — מהו? ופשיט התם: כיון דפסקה — פסקה, והויא מגורשת לעולם. ואם כן, גבי קדושין נמי הוי מקודשת לעולם, דאיתקש הויה ליציאה. וס"ד השתא דבהא לא פליג עולא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:1:1.english: "Today you are my wife and tomorrow you are not my wife, would she exit without a bill of divorce?" - And if you ask: From where do we know that she requires a bill of divorce? One can answer: In Chapter HaMegaresh in Gittin (83b), we raise a dilemma regarding one who says to his wife, "Today you are not my wife and tomorrow you are my wife" — meaning, you shall be divorced today, and tomorrow you shall not be divorced — what is [the law]? And [the Gemara] resolves there: Once he has severed [the marriage], he has severed [it], and she is divorced forever. And if so, regarding betrothal as well, she is betrothed forever, for betrothal (havayah) is equated with divorce (yetzi'ah). And we assume at this point that Ulla does not disagree regarding this.

Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:3:1.hebrew: והתנן שור זה עולה כל ל' יום עולה - ומועלין בה כל אותן שלשים יום — אור"י דגרס "דתניא", שהיא ברייתא ולא משנה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:3:1.english: "And didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]: 'This ox is a burnt-offering for all of thirty days' — [it is] a burnt-offering - and one is subject to the laws of misuse (me'ilah) with it all those thirty days" — Rabbi Yitzchak says that he reads [the text as] detanya ("And wasn't it taught"), for it is a baraita and not a Mishnah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:3:2.hebrew: שור זה עולה כל שלשים יום, ולאחר ל' יום שלמים, כל ל' יום עולה - ומועלין בה כל אותן ל' יום, [וגם] אם בא כל אותן ל' יום — מקריבו כדין עולה, ואם נתעכב להקריבו עד לאחר ל' יום, הוי משם ואילך שלמים. אלמא פקעה קדושת הגוף בכדי. ולא דמי להא דאמר בזבחים (דף ל -): "תחול זו ואח"כ תחול זו" — לא חיילא; דשאני הכא, דלכתחילה לא אמר סתם שיהיה עולה, אלא אמר: כל ל' יום:
Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:3:2.english: "This ox is a burnt-offering for all thirty days, and after thirty days a peace-offering — all thirty days it is a burnt-offering" - And it is subject to me'ilah [misuse of sacred property] all those thirty days, and also if one comes [to offer it] any time during those thirty days, he offers it according to the law of a burnt-offering, and if he delayed offering it until after thirty days, from then on it is a peace-offering. Thus, inherent sanctity departs with nothing [being done]. And this is not similar to that which [the Gemara] states in Zevachim (30): "[If one says,] 'Let this [sanctity] take effect and afterwards let this [other sanctity] take effect,' it does not take effect" — for here it is different, because initially he did not state without qualification that it should be a burnt-offering, rather he said "for all thirty days."

Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:4:1.hebrew: דאמר לדמי - שאמר לדמי עולה. וא"ת: והא אמרינן הקדיש זכר לדמיו, קדוש קדושת הגוף? וי"ל, דאיירי הכא דאמר לדמי נסכים, דמודה שם רבא, כדאמר בשבועות בפ"ק (דף יא -). אי נמי: התם בתם, ולכך קדוש קדושת הגוף; אבל הכא בבעל מום, ולכך קדוש קדושת דמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 29a:4:1.english: Where he said, "for [its] monetary value" - [That is,] he said, "for the monetary value of a burnt-offering." And if you will say: Do we not say [elsewhere] that if one consecrated a male [animal] for its monetary value, it is consecrated with physical sanctity? One can answer: Here [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where he said, "for the monetary value of libations," regarding which Rava agrees there, as he says in Shevuot in the first chapter (11a). Alternatively: there [it is speaking] of an unblemished [animal], and therefore it is consecrated with physical sanctity; whereas here [it is speaking] of a blemished [animal], and therefore it is consecrated [only] with monetary sanctity.
